system.name: WiseCode
system.one_liner: an erasure-coding system that scales wide-stripe vector codes to reach ultra-low storage overhead with low repair traffic

content.subject: the three-stage design process that turns coding parameters into a working vector-code encoding/decoding algorithm

content.key_idea: Realizing a vector code takes three sequential design steps—fix the coding structure, solve for valid coefficients, then build an encode/decode algorithm—each turning the previous step's output into a more concrete artifact.

summary: Figure 1 lays out the three sequential steps that WiseCode's paper says any vector code implementation must go through, moving from abstract parameters to a runnable algorithm. Starting from parameters (n, k, alpha), a Coding structure design box produces per-sub-stripe coding equations whose coefficients are still unknown, illustrated in a dashed callout with two example equations mixing blue data-chunk (d) and orange parity-chunk (p) terms against boxed placeholders. A Coefficient search box fixes those placeholders into valid, named coefficients (L0...L5) so the equations are decodable under any 1 to m-chunk failure, using the indices of which chunks are parity or lost. Finally, an Encoding/Decoding algorithm box turns the resolved equations into concrete arithmetic steps, shown solving for two parity values as weighted sums of data chunks. Bold red 'unknown' and 'valid' labels flag exactly what the middle stage changes.
summary_zh: 该图展示WiseCode实现向量码的三步骤：由参数经"结构设计"得系数未知方程（蓝=数据项，橙=校验项），再经"系数搜索"得有效系数，最后"编解码算法"给出求解步骤，红色标注unknown/valid的变化。
